newsitem.title: CHINA: China Eximbank to give $100 mln in buyer's credit.
newsitem.headline: China Eximbank to give $100 mln in buyer's credit.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of China will give $100 million in buyers' credits this year to boost exports of high-technology machinery and electronics, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

"China's export buyer's credit accounts for a small percentage of the total credit allocated to the machinery industry," the newspaper quoted the deputy general manager of the bank's credit department, Wang Bin, as saying.
China's hi-tech and value-added equipment exports accounted for only about 20 percent of total machinery and electronics sales abroad, the newspaper said.

The bank aimed to step up use of buyer's credits by expanding its range of financial services to include credit insurance and guarantees of Chinese government loans, the newspaper quoted Zou Xiaoyan, another official with the credit department, as saying.
The bank was discussing nine letters of intent for buyer's credit worth more than $400 million, the newspaper said but gave no further details.
China would step up its use of buyer's credits to help sellers avoid large debts and bring its financial sector more in line with those of Western nations, Zou said.
"Buyer's credit is often required in international bidding, expanded participation in which is eagerly sought by China," Zou said.
